Saving the Planet: 90's Style
A tribute to Captain Planet and the Planeteers - Created by Barbara Pyle and Ted Turner
Download from itch.io -
https://moonwolfv.itch.io/saving-the-planet-90s-style
​
Earth! Fire! Wind! Water! Ice!... Lightning?
Wait a minute, that doesn't sound right. Heart was in there somewhere, and wasn't there a Captain somewhere in all of this?
Six young adults have been presented with six elemental rings by the planet itself. In a world where many have become apathetic to anything regarding environmental awareness, where many are just trying to get by, these six - Celeste, Laura, Nina, James, Peter and Simon are the exception to the rule. Laura gets the ball rolling when she places a post on Farlbina University's message boards one night, and despite her fears that she might be the only one who still gives a care for the planet, she's quickly proven wrong. A few days later, a loud noise is heard right outside her house, and who should be there but Celeste, and her fusion-powered aircraft, the Geo Cruiser.
With the combination of their elemental rings and the power to travel anywhere on the planet thanks to the Geo Cruiser, these new Planeteers are soon facing the world's modern problems, ranging from your good old oil spills, sloppily managed Carbon Offset businesses, capitalists at their worst (Fraude Shakedon, I'm looking at you here), buildings constructed on the cheap, and lying PR spokespersons, and a monopoly on all the food and clothing on the planet.
With about six hours of game-play,  or more if you like things more challenging by not buying stat upgrades, Saving the Planet: 90's Style is for anyone who's a fan of Captain Planet and wants an RPG with a similar plot and somewhat familiar villains. Some of the Eco Villains out of Captain Planet get a small mention here and there.
Introducing the new planeteers:
Celeste:
Could well be described as "too clever for her own good". Her greatest achievement has been developing a fusion generator which is small enough that she can fit it into her Geo Cruiser, providing a means of environmentally friendly powered flight. She found her elemental ring while doing some maintenance on the wind turbines near her home town of Islisford.
Laura:
Sh
e's lived most of her life in the rural village of Aervis. She became greatly concerned about the rapid degradation of the soil in their fields. Things have become so bad that the soil can't grow anything on its own now, it's only CF seeds which can manage in it - And the more the CF seeds are used, the worse the soil quality gets.
Nina:
A volunteer firefighter from the city of Lapinberg. She found her ring in a burned-out building when she was searching for any remaining hot spots. Her ring could give her the powers to deal with many problems in a very quick, but smokey, fashion - She doesn't though, she cares greatly about air pollution and if she did, well, she could only call herself a lousy hypocrite.
James:
Com
es from the poor industrial town of Sumina. He may dress flashy but the truth of the matter is that he just knows how to spot an excellent bargain at a thrift store. He would have completely overlooked his ring if Laura didn't happen to just be in town on that afternoon.
Peter:
A keen surfer from the beach side town of La Turista. He doesn't indulge in his sport as much as he used to, as he spends more time clearing debris and other garbage which washes up on the beach. Puddles of oil have also made an appearance too, they seem to be coming from the recently opened DG Petrochemicals refinery.
Simon:
Hails
from the town of Kallby in the far north, and has become increasingly concerned by the slowly rising temperatures. When he found his ring, it was so cold he was wondering if he'd be able to get his fingers free of it.
Scenes from Saving the Planet: 90's Style
NOTE: For those familiar with Final Fantasy II, the world map is completely accessible right from the beginning of the game - point being: Only fight battles in the area you're meant to be in. Otherwise, battles will probably be much harder than they're meant to be.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Congrats on a completed game! I recall good times watching Captain Planet, and I think your description is written well.
There's really no reason to list every plugin and, like, every file in your project
It just creates three screens of useless info people have to scroll past to talk about your game. Even in the in-game credits (which you don't need to duplicate here) there's no need to list specific file names like that.
Good luck!

posts.author: MoonWolfV
posts.body:
Thanks ATT_Turan. I saw Archeia's post stating the rules for posting up a game and it seemed as though putting the credits in full was essential. Anyway, they're in a notepad  file included with the game.
I'll take out the credits out of the thread. Glad to hear it's not a necessity to have them in.
